title: 'Big Short' Michael Burry bets against AI stars Oracle, Nebius
excerpt: Michael Burry of "The Big Short" fame said on his Substack that he's shorting Oracle and Nebius, and several AI companies look vulnerable to him.
content_html:
Michael Burry says he's shorting AI stars Oracle and Nebius

By Theron Mohamed

You're currently following this author! Want to unfollow? Unsubscribe via the link in your email.

Michael Burry says he's shorting Oracle and Nebius, two companies that are betting big on the AI boom.

The investor of "The Big Short" fame said in a Substack post on Thursday that while researching the fourth part of a series titled "The Heretic's Guide to AI's Stars," he'd shorted the two stocks "because my work just wouldn't let me continue without doing so."

Writing broadly about AI companies, Burry compared them to fish in a barrel.

"The fish have gorged themselves on off-balance sheet liabilities. Backstops. Uncommenced leases. Purchase commitments," he wrote. "The fish have gotten very fat, very large, easy to shoot."

"Also, so large that it shan't be long before every last one keels over for lack of oxygen," he added.

Burry said he'd shorted Oracle stock at about $145. The enterprise-software giant's shares soared from below $130 to nearly $350 between April and September last year, as the AI boom fueled strong demand for its cloud infrastructure.

But they've tumbled nearly 60% since then on mounting concerns that Oracle has taken on too much debt during its data-center buildout.

As for Nebius, Burry said he'd shorted it "in somewhat larger size" at around $212 a share. The AI cloud infrastructure company's stock fell 13% to $190 on Thursday, but rallied 5% in Friday's premarket.

Nebius shares have still more than doubled this year, and have leaped roughly ninefold within the past two years.

Oracle, Nebius, and Burry didn't immediately respond to requests for comment from Business Insider.

'Bit of a pickle'

Burry has been one of the most vocal skeptics of the AI buildout, warning that Big Tech companies are overinvesting in microchips and data centers that could quickly become outdated.

In contrast, bulls point to the rapid growth rates at AI companies and say they're only getting started.

Oracle's remaining performance obligations, a measure of total future contract revenue, soared 363% to $638 billion in the year ended May 31.

Nebius' revenue soared nearly sevenfold year-on-year in the first quarter to almost $400 million. Its deferred revenue surged by around 150% over three months to $686 million on March 31.

Burry is best known for predicting and profiting from the collapse of the mid-2000s housing bubble. His contrarian wager was chronicled in the book and movie "The Big Short." He pivoted from running a hedge fund to writing about his personal investments late last year.

He's been negative on Oracle for many months, writing in a recent comment on his Substack, Cassandra Unchained, that it "does seem to be in a bit of a pickle."

"This might be the most expensive tragic fall for a very long time, a Homeresque own goal by a modern deity," he wrote. "Did not have to be this way."

Burry said in an August 4 post that he'd exited a bearish wager he'd placed against Oracle using put options. "The profit there was substantial, and so I left it at that," he wrote, adding that less volatility might prompt him to buy fresh puts.

Back in January, Burry said in a post that he owned bearish puts on Oracle stock and had shorted it during the second half of 2025. He explained that he didn't like the company's positioning and its investments, and found its AI strategy to be inexplicable and unnecessary.

In the chat thread for his latest post, he wrote that Nebius faces a "ton of execution risk" given the high costs and long leases in the data center business, and the difficulty of winning long-term commitments from customers.

迈克尔·伯里 (Michael Burry) 表示，他正在做空人工智能明星甲骨文 (Oracle) 和 Nebius

作者：Theron Mohamed 您目前正在关注该作者！ 想要取消关注吗？ 通过电子邮件中的链接取消订阅。

迈克尔·伯里 (Michael Burry) 表示，他正在做空甲骨文 (Oracle) 和 Nebius 两家公司，这两家公司在人工智能热潮上下了大注。

这位因“大空头”而出名的投资者周四在 Substack 的一篇文章中表示，在研究题为“人工智能之星的异端指南”系列的第四部分时，他做空了这两只股票，“因为我的工作不允许我继续这样做。”

伯里广泛地描述了人工智能公司，并将它们比作桶里的鱼。

“这些鱼已经吞噬了表外负债。 后挡板。 未开始的租赁。 购买承诺，”他写道。 “鱼已经变得很肥、很大，很容易拍摄。”

“而且，它太大了，用不了多久，最后一艘就会因为缺氧而倒下，”他补充道。

Burry 表示，他以约 145 美元的价格做空了 Oracle 股票。 去年 4 月至 9 月期间，这家企业软件巨头的股价从低于 130 美元飙升至近 350 美元，因为人工智能的繁荣刺激了对其云基础设施的强劲需求。

但自那以后，由于人们越来越担心甲骨文在数据中心扩建期间承担了过多的债务，股价已下跌近 60%。

至于 Nebius，伯里表示，他以每股 212 美元左右的价格“以更大的规模”做空了它。 这家人工智能云基础设施公司的股价周四下跌 13% 至 190 美元，但周五盘前上涨 5%。

Nebius 的股价今年仍然上涨了一倍多，并且在过去两年内上涨了大约九倍。

甲骨文、Nebius 和 Burry 没有立即回应《商业内幕》的置评请求。

“有点泡菜”

伯里一直是人工智能建设最强烈的怀疑者之一，他警告说，大型科技公司在微芯片和数据中心上过度投资，而这些技术可能很快就会过时。

相比之下，看多者指出人工智能公司的快速增长，并表示它们才刚刚开始。

在截至 5 月 31 日的财年中，甲骨文的剩余履约义务（衡量未来合同总收入的指标）飙升了 363%，达到 6,380 亿美元。

Nebius 第一季度的收入同比飙升近七倍，达到近 4 亿美元。 截至 3 月 31 日，其递延收入在三个月内飙升约 150%，达到 6.86 亿美元。

伯里因预测 2000 年代中期房地产泡沫的破裂并从中获利而闻名。 他的逆向赌注被记录在书籍和电影《大空头》中。 去年年底，他从经营一家对冲基金转向撰写个人投资文章。

几个月来，他一直对 Oracle 持负面态度，最近在他的 Substack Cassandra Unchained 评论中写道，它“似乎确实有点麻烦”。

他写道：“这可能是很长一段时间以来最昂贵的悲剧性坠落，是现代神灵的家乡式乌龙球。” “本来不必这样。”

Burry 在 8 月 4 日的一篇帖子中表示，他已经退出了使用看跌期权对甲骨文进行的看跌押注。 他写道：“那里的利润相当可观，所以我就这样了。”他补充说，波动性较小可能会促使他买入新的看跌期权。

早在一月份，伯里就在一篇帖子中表示，他持有甲骨文股票的看跌看跌期权，并在 2025 年下半年做空了该股票。 他解释说，他不喜欢该公司的定位和投资，并发现其人工智能战略莫名其妙且没有必要。

在他最新帖子的聊天线程中，他写道，鉴于数据中心业务的高成本和长期租约，以及赢得客户长期承诺的难度，Nebius 面临着“大量的执行风险”。
